collected.source: the lab’s own 5-minute XRP candles (no keys, no external fetch)
collected.window: XRP bars ordered by timestamp; boundary bars are those opening on the quarter-hour (:00/:15/:30/:45), scored against the off-grid bars around them
collected.pipeline: order bars by timestamp → mark quarter-hour boundary bars → last boundary bar’s return, volume burst vs the off-grid median, sign persistence across recent boundary bars → conditional bias

checks.name: data health
checks.detail: the XRP bar series read cleanly from the lab’s own candles

checks.name: history depth
checks.detail: enough bars and boundary bars on record — the clock-grid measurement is honest

checks.name: boundary read
checks.detail: the grid whispered: burst 1.16x the off-grid norm, sign persistence 25% across the last boundary bars — too faint or too scattered to license a tilt, so I keep it at zero rather than amplify noise

checks.name: out-of-sample edge
checks.detail: no scored forecasts yet — the scoreboard is still warming up

finding: The grid ticked, but faintly or in scattered directions — no burst worth the name, or boundary bars disagreeing with each other. Forcing a tilt out of that would be noise dressed as punctuality, so I abstain.
verdict_why: My rule is conditional by design: the boundary licenses a read only when it arrives with volume and agreement. A quiet grid says nothing, and I repeat nothing.

math_effect.detail: No mathematical effect on the forecast — my member weight is 0, so I am scored but never blended in.
